# vantage.ai. ## See and control what your coding agent does. Vantage is a free, open-source cost and usage monitor, guardrail and session log for coding agents. Launch tags:Software Engineering•Developer Tools•GitHub. Render: Get up to $100K in startup credits. Render: Get up to $100K in startup creditsCloud infrastructure for founders who want to move fast and NOT break things. is this more of a review after the fact, or can I actually block a change before it happens? the "control" part is what I'm curious about. being open source is the right call for something that sits between an agent and your keys, nobody should have to trust a closed binary for that. question on the guardrail side: does it block the action before the agent reads the secret, or does it let the read happen and just flag it in the session log after the fact? for us the scary case isn't the agent leaking a key in its output, it's the agent quietly using a live key to hit a paid API in a loop, so catching it before the call matters more than logging it afterward. The .env secret detection is the thing that got me, that's such a real footgun with coding agents and nobody was catching it. Congrats on the launch, this fills a gap that's been quietly costing people money and security for a while now. No reviews yetBe the first to leave a review for vantage.ai.

results.content:
Title: shim-cli: See what your coding agent sends. Mask what you can. | Product Hunt
## See what your coding agent sends. An open-source hook and local proxy for Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI and VS Code. In Claude Code it masks secrets and personal data in tool results before the model reads them, and shim watch shows what a session sent and cost. ### What shim-cli can't do. * A prompt you type into Claude Code or Codex is not masked, because neither client lets a hook rewrite it. Copilot CLI is the exception: there the model gets the masked prompt. * In Claude Code, the output of a failed command can't be replaced. A hook sits on the client's own tool calls, so it sees those too. shim-cli started with a question we couldn t answer: what does a coding agent actually send to the model? In Claude Code, a local hook masks secrets and personal data in tool results before the model reads them. When the agent opens a .env, the keys in it go to the model too, and nothing in the session tells you. shim-cli sits next to the agent you already use and runs on your machine:. • shim watch -- claude runs one session through a local proxy and prints where the input tokens went, what the session cost (or would cost on an API key), and which sensitive values were in the request and the response. • In Claude Code, shell commands, the output of a failed command and files attached with @ are reported, not masked. • Codex and Copilot CLI tool traffic is not inspected, and VS Code only reports. The one that surprised me most on my own machine was the output of a failed command: if a command fails, Claude Code doesn't let a hook replace its output, so cat .env && cat missing-file reaches the model as is. @mertcansaglam We run Claude Code on our own code every day, so seeing what a session actually sends, and what it cost, is the part I'd run first. shim-cli runs as a hook inside the agent itself, on your machine, so it only steps in at tool calls: it checks what a tool returns before the model gets it.
